title: trace-breadcrumbs-and-sli-storyboard-notes
content:
Purpose:
This note proposes a lightweight, human-friendly 'trace breadcrumb' pattern and an accompanying SLI storyboard to accelerate incident investigations for inference regressions (latency, cost spikes, quality anomalies). The goal is to make traces readable by product engineers and oncall responders without requiring deep familiarity with span internals.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Current traces are high-fidelity but noisy: many short spans, variable naming, and binary flags make it hard to quickly surface the causal chain for inference failures.
- Dashboard drilldowns often expose either only metrics or raw spans; bridging the two requires manual correlation.
- Investigations frequently chase expensive tail cases when a compact narrative could point to the root (KV cache miss avalanche, model fallback, tokenization mismatch).

High-level proposal:
1) Define a small set of breadcrumb events (semantic markers) that are emitted as lightweight annotations at key points in the inference path. Breadcrumbs are structured but human-readable strings attached to traces and logs.
2) Standardize span names and attributes for the most common inference steps so visualization surfaces consistent anchors.
3) Add an SLI 'storyboard' widget to dashboards: a curated sequence of metric+breadcrumb snapshots that describe the user-visible symptom and the most-likely causal signals.
4) Adopt a sampling and retention profile that keeps full traces for a small percentage of requests and breadcrumb-only traces for a larger population to reduce cost.

Breadcrumb taxonomy (recommended minimal set):
- request.start: request accepted by gateway (attrs: route, api_key_tier, model_family)
- route.resolve: routing decision (attrs: routing_policy, fallback_reason?)
- model.load-check: model version/quantization check (attrs: model_id, version, quantized=true/false)
- kv-cache.lookup: cache lookup attempt (attrs: key_hit=true/false, prefix_len)
- batch.enqueue: request batched (attrs: batch_size, batching_delay_ms)
- inference.exec: kernel dispatch (attrs: exec_backend=gpu|cpu, kernel_variant)
- tool.call: external tool invocation (attrs: tool_name, latency_ms, success)
- response.finish: finalization and response size (attrs: tokens_out, billed_tokens)
- anomaly.flag: automatic heuristic flag (attrs: reason=latency|quality|cost, score=0-1)

Notes on attributes: keep breadcrumb attributes to small categorical values and integers to keep event size tiny. Breadcrumbs should be emitted synchronously to the trace/span and replicated to the lightweight request-log index (for fast query).

Suggested span naming conventions (short, consistent):
- gateway.request
- router.resolve
- fetch.model-metadata
- cache.kv-lookup
- batch.window
- executor.invoke
- tool.{name}
- response.serialize

SLI Storyboard widget (dashboard wireframe described in prose):
- Top row: symptom selector (latency P99, error rate, hallucination rate) + time window selector.
- Middle row: metric sparkline + anomaly band (green/amber/red) and quick cohort selector (model, route, tenant).
- Bottom row: Storyboard lanes (3 lanes):
  * Breadcrumb timeline (compact timeline showing recent breadcrumb events counts; hover expands sample breadcrumbs with attributes)
  * Representative trace excerpt (sampled full trace with highlighted breadcrumb anchors)
  * Quick actions (links to saved trace queries, to open a canary roll, to re-run prompt tests)
- Interaction: clicking a breadcrumb filters metrics to that cohort and opens a set of example traces.

Sampling and retention strategy (cost-aware):
- Full trace retention: 0.5% of all requests (biased sampling to tail latency and anomaly.flag events). Retain full traces for 30 days.
- Breadcrumb-only traces: 10% of requests plus all requests marked anomaly.flag. Retain breadcrumb logs for 90 days in cheaper index.
- Short-lived ledger (7 days): aggregated breadcrumb counts and simple histograms per route/model to power the storyboard sparkline.

Cost model example (back-of-envelope):
- Assume 10M requests/day. Full-trace @ 0.5% -> 50k full traces/day. Estimated storage + indexing for full traces ~ 3 GB/day = ~90 GB/month.
- Breadcrumb-only @ 10% -> 1M breadcrumb entries/day. Small index, ~0.5 GB/day = ~15 GB/month.
- These are rough; validate with current trace size profile and storage tier pricing before adoption.

Instrumentation guidance (incremental rollout):
1) Implement breadcrumb emitters in the gateway and router layers first. Keep breadcrumbs as a small JSON blob (name, timestamp, attrs).
2) Add breadcrumb forwarding to request-log index (separate table/index optimized for time-series queries).
3) Standardize span names in the executor and batch layers. Add lightweight assertions to tests that confirm span name/attrs present.
4) Integrate anomaly.flag heuristics from Optimize monitoring and wire them into breadcrumbs.
5) Build the storyboard dashboard using existing dashboard platform (Grafana/LlamaDash placeholder) as a custom panel that queries both metrics and breadcrumb index.

Investigation play examples (how this helps):
- Latency tail: breadcrumb timeline shows a spike in kv-cache.lookup miss=true for the same route and model -> investigate cache eviction policy and cold-start patterns.
- Model fallback: route.resolve breadcrumb shows fallback_reason=capacity and then inference.exec with kernel_variant=small-quant -> causal chain visible, roll back routing, re-evaluate burst capacity.
- Hallucination spike: anomaly.flag=quality aligned with tool.call success=false and response.serialize shorter token_out -> points to external tool degradation.

Acceptance criteria for rollout phase 1 (MVP):
- Breadcrumb events emitted for gateway.request, route.resolve, kv-cache.lookup, inference.exec and response.finish across 90% of traffic for the beta routes.
- Storyboard dashboard renders breadcrumb timeline and links into at least one full trace sample.
- Sampling pipeline stores breadcrumb index and full traces at the configured sampling rates.
- Oncall can reduce mean time to identifying root cause by at least 30% in runbook drills (measured via drill retros).

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How to reconcile tenant privacy/K-anonymity with breadcrumb attributes? We may need to mask tenant IDs in breadcrumb index for certain SKUs.
- If breadcrumb index becomes high-cardinality (free-form attrs), the cost will rise. Enforce attribute whitelists and enums.
- Do we need cross-service correlation IDs beyond request.id? Proposal: add request.session_id for multi-hop conversational flows.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Tech spike: prototype breadcrumb emitter in router for two beta routes (owner: Marco) by 2025-02-25.
- Dashboard spike: minimal storyboard panel hooking into breadcrumb index (owner: Sara) by 2025-03-10.
- Privacy review: quick pass to identify sensitive attributes (owner: Anya) by 2025-02-20.
- Cost validation: SRE to run trace size analysis for past 90 days (linked JIRA JIRA-OPS-589).

Appendix: sample breadcrumb JSON (tiny):
{ "name": "kv-cache.lookup", "ts": "2025-02-11T15:23:01Z", "attrs": "hit=false;prefix=auth-;route=chat-v1" }

Rationale for compactness: prefer a single compact attrs string (semi-colon delimited) in the breadcrumb index to keep indexing cheap. Full attribute dictionaries can remain in full traces.

Sign-off notes:
This is intentionally conservative: aim for high signal-to-noise and low cardinality. If the team endorses, we'll convert this into a lightweight instrumentation RFC that enumerates attribute enums and the sampling plumbing.
